newsitem.title: INDIA: India HDFC up 6 pct at National Exchange.
newsitem.headline: India HDFC up 6 pct at National Exchange.

text.p: Shares of India's Housing Development & Finance Company (HDFC) jumped 221.05 rupees, or six percent, to 3,966.05 at the National Stock Exchange on Monday after foreign funds turned buyers in the stock, traders said.
India's leading housing finance company on Friday said it had received central bank approval for foreign institutional investors (FIIs) to raise their holding limits to 30 percent from 24 percent.
HDFC shares hit a price limit at the NSE, with the stock attracting only buyers of 23,080 shares, traders said.

Disbursals made by HDFC rose 24 percent so far in 1997/98 (April-March) to 3.23 billion rupees against 2.61 billion in the same period last year, Deepak Parekh, HDFC chairman said at the company's annual shareholders meeting last week.
HDFC shares ended at 3,711.75 rupees at the BSE on Friday. The opening at the BSE was delayed on Monday due to a power crisis, exchange officials said.
